articleTitle: Segmentation of the Cervix in Colposcopy Images Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Cervical cancer caused by human Papillomavirus (HPV), a sexually transmitted disease, is one of the most common neoplasms in women nationally and globally. Although there are health campaigns promoting screening tests to detect the disease, the waiting times for results are high due to deficiencies in laboratory infrastructure, affecting diagnosis. In this work, we propose to apply machine learning techniques for cervical segmentation in colposcopy images obtained during cytology, more specifically the cervix region for supporting a further classification stage. Finally, we develop a desktop application only for unsupervised learning models. Also, this work is a result of the project CITOBOT, funded by Minciencias and developed by a multidisciplinary team. Results show acceptable metrics in the segmentation of the cervix, both in unsupervised and supervised methods.

articleTitle: Design of a Monitor for Harmful Gases in Hospital Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Indoor environmental quality, including thermal, acoustic, light and respirable air parameters, is critical to public health. Many people conduct more than 80% of their daily activities in indoor spaces, such as offices, educational institutions, and healthcare facilities. Air quality integrity is a determining factor for both safety and physiological well-being. In hospital environments, environmental pollutants emanate from medical procedures, inherent materials, equipment, and often inadequate ventilation infrastructures. Judicious air quality control in these places is essential to avoid immediate conditions such as eye irritation and fatigue and mitigate the long-term onset of respiratory diseases and neoplastic pathologies. Implementing rigorous surveillance systems and effective pollution reduction protocols is fundamental to safeguarding a healthy environment that promotes recovery and care delivery. This paper presents a monitor's design and conceptual model for carbon dioxide, particulate matter, temperature, and ambient humidity. In this case, the monitor's design and functional requirements and the sensors' sensitivities are established, considering the regulations that establish the limit values in closed environments. This conceptual model is susceptible to implementation, laboratory adjustments, and potential use as an air quality monitor in hospital environments.

articleTitle: Development of a Specialized Methodology for Custom Upper Limb Prosthesis Design in Cyclists
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: The growing number of upper limb amputations has highlighted the need for advanced prosthetic solutions, especially in specialized activities such as cycling. Current options for cyclists with transhumeral amputations often do not meet the necessary biomechanical and ergonomic requirements. This study proposes an innovative methodology for the personalized design of upper limb prostheses, based on an iterative process that includes 3D scanning and constant feedback from the athlete. Through a case study of a high-performance cyclist, a personalized coupling system was developed that was evaluated under training and competition conditions. In addition, stress and displacement analyses were performed to verify the structural integrity and the ability of the coupling to withstand the loads associated with cycling. The results confirmed that the design not only offers an optimal fit, but also stability and durability in real conditions. This methodology provides a promising, low-cost approach to the creation of sports prostheses that improve the performance and quality of life of cyclists with amputations.

articleTitle: Haptic Interfaces Integration in Upper Limb Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: The activities of daily living (ADLs) encompass self-care tasks that often rely on upper limb function. Stroke, or cerebrovascular accident (CVA), and musculoskeletal injuries (MSIs) can compromise these ADLs, necessitating rehabilitation therapy. However, many individuals exhibit poor adherence to prescribed therapies, which exacerbates their conditions and further impairs upper limb functionality. To tackle this challenge, we devised a software tool that integrates a mathematical model with haptic interfaces within a Unity-developed game for the Meta Quest 2 platform. Validation by physiotherapists indicated successful results, affirming its utility as an effective tool for upper limb rehabilitation therapy.

articleTitle: APPLEE: Automated Preprocessing Pipeline for Low-Electrode Encephalography
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is crucial for studying cortical neuronal activity in medical diagnostics and research. However, artifacts often contaminate low-density EEG recordings, necessitating careful preprocessing to ensure data reliability. This study introduces APPLEE (Automated Preprocessing Pipeline for Low-Electrode Encephalography), a novel preprocessing pipeline tailored to enhance data in low-density EEG recordings. APPLEE incorporates advanced techniques for artifact reduction, evaluated using data from two cohorts: high-density and low-density (8 electrodes). The results indicate that APPLEE allows the processing of reduced samples with as few as 8 high-density electrodes while preserving signal quality. Additionally, smaller standard deviations were observed in spectral estimations compared to the HAPPILEE pipeline (Harvard Automated Pre-processing Pipeline Include Low-Electrode Encephalography). This comparative analysis underscores APPLEE's innovative methodologies in addressing challenges specific to low-density EEG configurations, demonstrating improved performance in attenuating unwanted frequencies.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Personalized Stander for a Child with DiGeorge Syndrome: A Service-Learning Project in Biomedical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a personalized stander for a child with DiGeorge Syndrome, under-taken as a service-learning project in the Human Biomechanics course at Pontificia Universidad Javeriana Cali. The project was conducted in collaboration with Neuroprematuros, a neurodevelopment program in Cali, aiming to create a device tailored to the specific needs of a boy with hypotonia and genetic deterioration. The methodology involved Quality Function Deployment (QFD) to translate user needs into engineering specifications, resulting in a custom stander that supports the child's physical therapy at home. The stander includes features such as adjustable support points, lockable wheels, and a folding mechanism for ease of transport. The project demonstrates the significant impact of integrating academic knowledge with real-world applications, contributing to the well-being of the child and his family while enhancing the learning experience of biomedical engineering students.

articleTitle: Methodology for the Validation of Competencies and Skills Associated with the Safe Use of Biomedical Technology at the University Hospital Fundación Valle Del Lili
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)

authors.preferredName: Daniel Ernesto De La Cruz López

abstract: This project presents the development of a methodology for validating competencies and skills associated with the safe use of biomedical technology for healthcare personnel at the University Hospital Fundación Valle del Lili. In this project, a methodology was developed for validating the competencies and skills associated with the safe use of biomedical technology by medical and healthcare personnel at the University Hospital Fundación Valle del Lili. The aim was to strengthen the training program, contribute to patient safety, and reduce the incidence of reports associated with the incorrectly use of biomedical equipment. Initially, a diagnosis and analysis of the training program were carried out. Based on the findings, the most appropriate method for evaluating the impact of training on medical and healthcare personnel was determined, and the methodology was designed. Subsequently, the biomedical equipment and personnel profiles were selected through statistical sampling, and the methodology was applied in a pilot test. Finally, the results were shared with the institution, and a procedure was developed to implement the methodology as an institutional policy.

articleTitle: Automatic Silence Detection Employing Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Context Analyses
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Automated speech and pause/silence detection is a crucial task in clinical and pathological environments, supporting diagnostic processes and providing essential information for treatment planning. This study evaluates three methods for automatic silence detection in clinical speech analysis: (1) a traditional energy-based method using zero-crossing detection, (2) a pretrained neural network model for voice activity detection (Silero-VAD), and (3) NVIDIA's speaker diarization and transcription tool. All methods demonstrated effective pause/silence detection with comparable error rates, though Silero-VAD exhibited superior precision and performance. Key metrics included a Dice coefficient of 0.917, an onset error of 500 ms, and an endpoint error of 370 ms, highlighting the importance of audio preprocessing.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques for Hand Gesture Recognition Using Surface Electromyography
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Hand gesture recognition for the control of rehabilitation and assistive technologies is still a field to be explored. This study investigated the effectiveness of different methods for classifying hand gestures using surface electromyography (sEMG) signals collected from the upper Thalmic Myo armband in experiment two of the Ninapro 5 database. Initially, traditional Machine Learning (ML) techniques were applied, an extraction of temporary characteristics was made, and dimensionality reduction through Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by four classical classifiers, Decision Trees (DT), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Bayes-Gaussian (NBG) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). However, the results were unsatisfactory, with a maximum accuracy of only 0.10. Subsequently, Deep Learning (DL) techniques were adopted, where the sEMG signals were transformed into images through the Fourier Transform, and although they showed a significant improvement, with a training accuracy of approximately 0.90, the accuracy in validation and testing remained around 0.50. This indicates possible overtraining issues and a lack of differentiation between classes of images. Despite these challenges, DL proved superior to ML in classifying hand gestures from sEMG signals. It is concluded that further research and improvement of signal-to-image transformation techniques are needed to achieve more accurate and feasible classification in real-time applications.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Dual-Task and Brain Activity Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Continuous monitoring of a patient's health is a critical challenge in modern healthcare and has become a popular telehealth option. For neurodegenerative diseases, such monitoring is crucial for early detection and intervention. Technology plays an important role in healthcare by enabling earlier disease diagnosis and promoting healthy aging. Electroencephalography (EEG) is a low-cost, portable, and non-invasive technique that allows the study of brain function and physiological changes associated with neurodegenerative processes. Dual-task assessments provides valuable insights into the cognitive state of individuals. Both techniques are non-invasive and portable, making them highly accessible and practical. In this study, we developed and implemented a protocol for simultaneous dual-task and EEG assessment, combining cognitive tasks with motor tasks involving elbow flexion a nd e xtension. W e s imultaneously r ecorded EEG activity and kinematic variables of the movement and calculated the dual-task cost. Our findings show that this framework facilitated the acquisition of accurate and consistent data, allowing a description of the effects of dual-tasking on the measured variables.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a System to Wake Up People with Hearing Loss Based on Biodesign Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Hearing loss represents 20% of the world's population, while in Colombia this condition reaches the 1,2%. It is a condition in which activities of daily living, such as waking up in the morning, can become a challenge. Some technologies have been implemented but difficulties such as the adaptability of the equipment, comfort regarding device design and effectiveness of the technology to wake the user remain in its use. Part of the success in the use of these technologies lies in a good needs identification stage, as is recommended for the Biodesign framework, a methodology to design and build health technologies. This work presents the design and development of an alternative system for the comfortable awakening of people with hearing loss, using the Biodesign methodology. The system obtained includes a tabletop device and a wireless portable instrument, with visual and tactile stimulation respectively. Preliminary results obtained show that the system is viable, and responds to basic needs identified.

articleTitle: Subject-Specific Pre-Processing Pipeline for EEG Artifact Removal Aimed at Enhancing SSVEP Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Steady-State Visually Evoked Potentials (SSVEP) based Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) offer significant potential in assistive and rehabilitation technologies. However, the performance of SSVEP detection is often compromised by artifacts in Electroencephalography (EEG) signals and inter-subject variability, among other factors. This study introduces a subject-specific p reprocessing p ipeline a imed a t enhancing SSVEP signal detection accuracy. The proposed method involves a dual-stage approach, utilizing EEG signals recorded both during a baseline rest state and during tasks known to induce artifacts. By establishing a personalized reference for each subject, the pipeline enables more accurate artifact detection and removal. The pipeline's efficacy w as e valuated u sing Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) on an open EEG dataset, with performance assessed across varying time segments (1, 2, 3 y 4 s). Detection accuracy was calculated to quantify performance in SSVEP detection. The performance of the proposed method for the 4-second time segment was superior (96.44%) compared to the standard method (93.78%). The results demonstrate the pipeline's potential to improve the reliability of SSVEP-based BCIs, particularly in highly contaminated signals.

articleTitle: Customized 3D-Printed Prototype Mold for Potential HDR Brachytherapy in Facial Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Surface mold brachytherapy (SMBT) is an appropriate and effective treatment for non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC). Manual manufacturing methods allow the development of personalized molds. However, it causes inconsistencies in the dosimetry of the established treatment plan, mainly due to the air gaps between the patient dermal surface and the mold. This work is focused on developing a manufacturing methodology for a prototype of a custom mold through additive manufacturing for potential application in BT in patients with NMSC.

articleTitle: Estimation of Blood Pressure and Glucose through Photoplethysmography and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This article presents the development of a system for non-invasive measurement of blood pressure and glucose levels using photoplethysmography (PPG) and machine learning models. The system, called CARDIOPRESS, combines an optical sensor to capture heart rate and oxygen saturation (SpO2) data with machine learning algorithms to predict systolic and diastolic blood pressure, as well as blood glucose levels. Experimental results demonstrate a good approximation in the prediction of both blood pressure and glucose levels, validating its potential for continuous monitoring of cardiovascular and metabolic health.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Computational Intelligence System to Identify Respiratory Distress from Digital Signal Processing of Voice
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This paper presents a computational intelligence system that allows us to identify people with respiratory distress in an automatic and non-invasive way. This is accomplished through the digital signal processing techniques of voice, integrating the calculation of acoustic, spectral, temporal, and sta-tistical parameters and neural networks. The computational method is implemented in a client-server architecture that allows recording two sustained vowel sounds (vowel “a” and “o”) of a spanish-speaking population group aged between 18 and 49 years old. Results show that the vowel “a” is more efficient in women with a hit rate of 97.62% for detecting respiratory distress. In contrast, the vowel “o” is more efficient in men, reaching a hit rate of 96.77%. This system is expected to contribute to the development of novel support tools that could be used in the medical field to facilitate the diagnosis of respiratory diseases and prevent their spread.

articleTitle: Development of an Electronic Prototype for Stress Measurement Using Physiological Variables in School Teachers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Stress was identified as an innate response of the body to challenging and demanding situations, and it emerged as a growing concern in the workplace. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defined it as a global epidemic affecting workers of various ages and professions. Given this reality, the research presented here delved into the study of physiological signals, which were considered crucial indicators to determine the presence of stress. Using the Device for Detecting the Presence of Stress (DDPS), various physiological responses were recorded, including electrodermal activity (EDA), skin temperature (ST), and electrocardiography (ECG). Tests carried out in controlled environments confirmed that the DDPS's accuracy was on average 68 % in identifying episodes of stress in teachers.

articleTitle: Comparison of KNN and SVM Methods for Melanoma Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Melanomas are a type of skin cancer that have a high mortality rate, and early detection is essential to improve patient survival. This article presents a comparison between two machine learning algorithms, KNN and SVM, applied to image processing to classify lesions using images. The methodology of this project was divided into two parts: preprocessing and feature extraction. In the preprocessing, the images were segmented using the Otsu method. For feature extraction, the ABCD test was considered, analyzing the parameters of asymmetry, border, and color. Then, the two machine learning models were trained for comparison. The results showed an accuracy of 58.96% for KNN and 64.09% for SVM.

articleTitle: Segmentation and Identification of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis (MTB)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This article addresses the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) using digital image processing to enhance tuberculosis diagnosis. The microscopic-observation drugsusceptibility (MODS) method and computer vision strategies are employed, carrying out several preprocessing steps, such as grayscale conversion, binarization and morphological operations. Four computer vision models were trained, with the third model standing out for its accuracy by combining original images with segmented edges. This approach facilitates the rapid and accurate detection of bacilli, enhancing diagnosis and tuberculosis control.

articleTitle: Biomedical Equipment for the Measurement of Inspiratory and Expiratory Volumes Based on the Ubicu Respiratory Incentive
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: The increasing rates of restrictive respiratory diseases as a result of the consequences of COVID-19 in Colombia during the last three years have led to an increased implementation of lung reexpansion therapies, in order to treat and prevent the loss of lung volumes and capacities. There are different techniques to treat these problems, such as deep inspiration and respiratory incentives. Incentive physiotherapy is one of the techniques for the recovery of lung capacity that gives feedback to the patient about the volume or flow achieved. The Pontificia Universidad Javeriana Cali together with the Universidad del Valle designed the Ubicu respiratory incentive which is a system oriented to inspiration in lung reexpansion therapies along with the help of a gamified software that improved patient adherence. The objective of the project is to design and build a biomedical device to measure inspiratory and expiratory volume using a flow-volume sensor, determining the vital capacity of a healthy adult, seeking to enrich the qualities of the current Ubicu respiratory incentive. The design process was done with the use of TRIZ, Design Thinking and Axiomatic Design with an interdisciplinary team of the project. For the designed product, a primary plate-orifice sensor was used that allows the flow to be accurately measured in both directions, the management of the measurement and Bluetooth communication was done with the microcontroller ESP32, and the feedback with the UNITY platform. For the validation of the flow measurement, a reference system was used implementing the VT650 standard device and the CITREX H3 device, and the vital capacity was validated through tests with twelve healthy people, with an analogous basedline spirometer. It is concluded that the prototype built is an alternative to the current systems for measuring vital capacity and can be integrated into the current patient management system with greater performance than the current ones of inspired flow.

articleTitle: BrainView: A Novel Platform for Acquisition, Processing, and Warehouse of EEG Signals from a Portable Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Electroencephalographic (EEG) signal analysis has emerged as a promising tool for early diagnosis and continuous monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases. In recent years, portable technologies for EEG signal acquisition have gained significant attention due to their potential for continuous and non-invasive monitoring of brain activity in various contexts, ranging from clinical research to commercial and personal consumer applications. We aim to design and develop a platform that simplifies the acquisition, processing, and storage of EEG signals, improving monitoring of the progression and manifestation of neurodegenerative diseases in uncontrolled environments like clinical settings. BrainView is built in collaboration with healthcare professionals to ensure it meets needs and facilitates implementation in everyday practices. The methodology used includes the design of a scalable and easy-to-use platform that integrates processes for the acquisition, processing, and storage of EEG signals and demographic data. Highlights include the use of OpenBCI technology for signal capture and the application of filtering techniques to the acquired data. The results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of the platform in the acquisition and processing of EEG signals in real time, as well as its ability to store and manage data both locally and in the cloud. Usability testing indicates that the tool is intuitive even for non-specialist users, making it easy to adopt in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Bloodmeter: Application for Data Acquisition and Analysis in Diabetes Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: BLOODMETER is a comprehensive project that addresses doctor-patient communication and diabetes management through an innovative application. It began with a literature review supported by scientific evidence and a customized survey in Bogotá to understand specific needs. The app allows patients to monitor glucose levels and effectively share data with their doctors, demonstrating a positive impact on communication and disease control. BLOODMETER aims to enhance the quality of life for people with diabetes, strengthening the doctor-patient relationship for more effective, patient-centered healthcare.

articleTitle: UltraScan-S: Development of an Assistance Device for Lung Ultrasound Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: In Peru, respiratory diseases, particularly pneumonia, are highly prevalent, with a notably prevalence in rural areas where the limited availability of specialized medical personnel hinders early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Early detection and proper assessment are critical for improving patient outcomes, yet access to reliable diagnostic tools remains a challenge in these underserved regions. In this work, an assistive device is developed to automate the pressure applied by the linear ultrasound transducer, using image parameters to control the force exerted on the body. The device is compatible with a Point of Care Ultrasound (POCUS) methodology, which involves capturing images in a point-by-point manner for immediate assessment. UltraScan-S aims to enhance the quality of images obtained at specific points, ensuring a more accurate diagnosis. The results demonstrate that UltraScan-S enables the acquisition of images by maintaining the proper balance between image quality and the applied force on the skin, with a maximum force of 20 N, ensuring it is not harmful. Additionally, the device allows individuals with basic knowledge of POCUS to obtain high-quality images, thus contributing to more effective and accessible diagnostics in resource-limited settings

articleTitle: Identification of Alterations in Surgical Wounds Through the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Digital Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Globally, surgical site infections are common complications that are both serious and costly. While telemedicine has enhanced the remote assessment of surgical wounds, it still faces limitations. This study introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) model designed to automatically classify digital images of surgical wounds as either altered or unaltered. The study utilized a dataset of 4,262 segmented and expert-labeled images. The CNN model achieved an accuracy of 83.46%, a sensitivity of 81.54%, and an AUROC of 92.22%. Although the MobileNet model demonstrated acceptable performance, it was less effective in comparison. The findings s uggest t hat C NNs a re e ffective for classifying images of surgical wounds, with potential for further improvement using advanced techniques and a multidisciplinary expert panel.

articleTitle: Innovation in Motion: Characterization of Running in a Paralympic Athlete Undergoing Adaptation to a Transradial Prosthesis Benefiting Stability and Symmetry of Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: In paralympic athletics, the use of adaptations or prosthetics is heavily influenced by the resources available to athletes. The high cost of these adaptations, combined with limited detailed methodologies for creating personalized orthopedic devices, presents a significant challenge. This study addresses these issues by presenting the design, development, and biomechanical evaluation of a transradial prosthesis tailored for a 27-year-old female paralympic track and field athlete with an upper limb amputation. The primary objective is to optimize the athlete's performance by addressing both kinetic and kinematic factors, particularly during running and the starting position. The research outlines the comprehensive process, including the residual limb's scanning, the socket's design, and the iterative development of prosthesis prototypes using materials such as thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and polylactic acid (PLA). Key findings indicate improvements in shoulder alignment, enhanced balance during the starting position, and increased symmetry in plantar pressure distribution. The proposed methodology, which leverages 3D technologies, underscores the importance of ongoing analysis to monitor the athlete's adaptation to the prosthesis and its impact on her athletic performance. This approach demonstrates the potential for personalized prosthetic solutions to significantly enhance athletic outcomes in paralympic sports.

articleTitle: CNN-LSTM Proposal for Colombian Sign Language Greetings Classification: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Colombian sign language (CSL) have shown different advances to automatize the translation and communication between deaf or disabling hearing people and speakers. However, these current efforts are oriented on classification of static signs, mainly. The present proposal implements the use a convolutional neural network (CNN) that also involves the use an architecture of the long short-term memory (LSTM) one. This allowed to include the time dependent information for dynamic signs like a sequence data. For this, a dataset was created with greetings for the CSL through the recording videos of signs. The methodology used the MediaPipe tool for feature extraction, which was used to represent relevant points from fingers articulation for frames of the videos. CNN-LSTM was applied with the joint points information for the classification. Results show that 71.50 % (+/-4.33%) for five greetings classification, employing a crossvalidation and early stopping criteria for the training of models.

articleTitle: Characterization of Water with Added Salt using Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: A permittivity sensor is used to measure the dielectric properties of water in the microwave range. The tests are performed without direct physical contact between the sensor and the samples. The results obtained show that it is possible to identify different levels of salinity in water with an inexpensive and simple method.

articleTitle: Smartwatch-Based IoT System for Continuous Intravenous Infusion Monitoring with Air Bubble Blockage
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Manual monitoring of intravenous (IV) infusions can result in errors or interruptions, particularly in healthcare settings with limited resources. This study introduces an Internet of Things (IoT)-based system designed to enhance the safety and efficiency of IV by enabling continuous, remote, and real-time monitoring. The proposed system integrates devices to measure fluid levels, detect blockages, and automatically prevent air bubbles from entering the bloodstream. Alerts are transmitted to healthcare professionals via smartwatches, ensuring prompt interventions. The system's efficacy was substantiated through calculations and laboratory tests, demonstrating its capacity to maintain precise fluid delivery and minimize the risk of medical errors. This innovative approach not only optimizes patient care but also reduces the workload on healthcare staff by automating routine monitoring tasks, thereby representing a significant advancement in healthcare technology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Impedance Vector Trajectory when Applying Physical Effort: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Collection of clinical evidence is needed for timely diagnosis and specialized patient monitoring. Likewise, bioimpedance analysis is key in obtaining information about body composition, thus, the bioimpedance vector is used to evaluate a patient's metabolic condition. This study proposes to assess the effects of a daily exercise routine on body composition using the bioimpedance vector. Also, the impedance magnitude, the phase angle, and short-term changes are graphically and statistically analyzed. Thus, the bioimpedance vector is plotted as a function of resistance and reactance to observe the behavior of cellular mass and body water. Results show significant differences in impedance over time (p=0.0001) related to changes in the quantity and distribution of body fluids and different types of mass, which can be useful for evaluating the effects of nutrition, sports training, rehabilitation therapies, as well as contributing to timely medical diagnosis in further studies.

articleTitle: Prototype Simulator as a Tool to Support Training in the Surgical Technique of Extracapsular Cataract Extraction in Canines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Cataracts are a frequent cause of blindness in canines, and their timely diagnosis and treatment are crucial to preserve the animal's quality of life. Although surgery is the primary treatment, its success depends on the surgeon's skill; the extracapsular extraction technique, one of the most commonly used, presents intraoperative complications since cadaver training does not adequately replicate the ocular biomechanical properties. A simulator prototype has been developed for the training of this technique, which allows realistic practices and improves professional competence. The development involved the characterization of the eye and the surgical technique using a bibliographic and experimental review, as well as a biomechanical analysis of the eye considering the forces generated by the extraocular muscles and the force required for the initial incision in the sclera (2.36 N), which an electronic system will measure during the procedure. In the design stage, CAD tools, 3D printing, and casting techniques were used to obtain the parts that simulate the tissues, the mesocephalic head of the canine, and strain gauges were used to measure the force set using a Wheatstone bridge. A first evaluation showed improvements in terms of size and arrangement of the interchangeable parts.

articleTitle: System for Data Acquisition and Measurement of Muscle Strength Using EMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal for an interactive prototype that utilizes electromyographic signals (EMG) along with the force hammer game to measure and enhance muscular strength in a fun and motivating manner. It is based on research on the Neuromuscular System, emphasizing the significance of EMG signals in monitoring muscle groups affected by injuries or pathologies. The construction of the final system includes an EMG module and a vu-meter to create a force measurement tool. The proposal is developed after reviewing devices that acquire muscle signals controlled by the nervous system. The main objective is to implement a data acquisition system that measures muscular strength through the force hammer game. The document details the stages of prototype development, from identifying design opportunities to planning the implementation of the functional prototype. The importance of following established stages is emphasized, underscoring the applicability of the prototype in various scenarios. The prototype stands out for its ability to provide visual feedback and improve the measurement and application of force and movements. It is considered a valuable tool in processes such as rehabilitation, facilitating the optimal recovery of the patient.

articleTitle: Innovative Simulation Training Model for Cataract Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Cataracts significantly impair vision and are predominantly treated through surgery, specifically phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation. Training residents in cataract surgery is essential for medical schools. This article outlines the initial development stages of a cataract surgery training model, detailing the methodology, including a comprehensive literature review, surgical practice analysis, and the creation of prototypes that accurately mimic ocular structures and textures. The model underwent validation by ophthalmologists, who offered feedback on its accuracy and realism. The validation results and the identified opportunities for enhancement are discussed. The iterative development approach enabled the replication of realistic surgical conditions, thereby improving the tools and techniques used in training cataract surgery residents.

articleTitle: Development of a Prototype for the Prevention of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Based on EMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a project for the prevention of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), a common peripheral neuropathy in people exposed to repetitive hand movements. A prototype is proposed that detects repetitive movements in the wrist muscles, offering a non-invasive alternative to avoid surgical interventions and preserve work functionality. The methodology combines engineering principles with Design Thinking tools, facilitating an iterative and coordinated approach at all stages of the project. The results show the signals obtained from the design and implementation of the EMG signal acquisition system and the tests performed on different wrist muscles. Finally, it concludes with the achievements of the project and discusses the importance of the structured methodology in the development of the prototype, while identifying opportunities for improvement, such as the integration of the systems into a wearable bracelet, and discussing possible future work, such as the development of a native alarm system through an application.

articleTitle: Development of a Skin Simulator Prototype for Suture Practice in Collaboration with Pereira Rossell Hospital Center
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This work addresses the need to create a prototype skin simulator for suture practice training for medical students at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center (CHPR). Based on the evaluation of materials used in commercially available models in the Uruguayan market, the goal was to scale the prototype using two initial materials: resin and silicone rubber, analyzing resin curing failures under a microscope. The final choice of silicone rubber was selected due to its similarity to human skin, validated through tensile testing and reviewed by expert surgeons. The simulator, manufactured by depositing silicone rubber onto a mold designed and modeled using 3D printing technologies, provides adequate realism for suture practice in a simulated clinical setting.

articleTitle: Injectable Hydrogel Based on Oxidized Agarose–Carboxymethyl Chitosan with Potential Use in Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: A hydrogel based on carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCh) and oxidized agarose (OA) was prepared and characterized by evaluating properties such as gelation, injectability, syringeability, mechanical properties, self-healing capacity, and swelling ratio. The hydrogel has a stable gel consistency at 37 °C. However, it could be injected through a 21 G-gauge needle with a maximum force of 18.37 ± 1.4 N. Also, applying a load of 18.24 N for 15 s gave a syringeability percentage of 54.08 ± 3.73%, indicating good injection performance. The hydrogel exhibited a compressive strength of 46.28 ± 7.44 kPa and a Young's modulus of 8.67 ± 0.73 kPa, indicating the formation of a flexible crosslinked network. Additionally, it was observed that storage at 4 °C can alter the previously mentioned properties. Finally, it was found that the hydrogel can self-repair after 48 h and swell up to 2 530 ± 388% in 15 days. Considering this, the obtained hydrogel has the potential to be implemented in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Advancements in Fourth-Generation Endodontic Apex Locators for Enhanced Precision in Root Canal Treatments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This paper presents the comprehensive development and validation of an electronic apex locator designed specifically for endodontic treatments in Cochabamba, Bolivia. The device utilizes advanced impedance measurement techniques to accurately determine the position of dental files within root canals. By integrating cutting-edge electronic technology with specialized dental knowledge, this project aims to significantly enhance the precision and efficiency of root canal treatments in the region. The system incorporates a user-friendly interface, real-time data processing, and multiple output modalities. Extensive experimental results demonstrate high accuracy and repeatability in locating the root apex, validating its potential to substantially improve endodontic procedures and contribute to better oral health outcomes in the local population.

articleTitle: Detection of Artifacts in Mammographic Images Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Accurate detection and classification of artifacts in mammographic images is critical in diagnosing and following breast pathologies. Artifacts generated during mammogram capture and caused by software processing errors or detector problems can distort image interpretation and compromise diagnostic accuracy. This work implements artifact detection, specifically two artifacts related to the mammogram unit: Contrast Splatter (CS) and White Pixel (WP). A state-of-the-art convolutional neural network was used to detect and classify the data: YOLOV8. Tests were run in the modified database from CBIS-DDSM, where artifacts were synthetically added according to actual parameters reported in the bibliography. Results show promising results using YOLOV8, with a 0.95 and 0.97 recall index for CS y WP, respectively. However, other metrics show low accuracy and precision performance for WP detection. This work shows the usability of artificial intelligence methods in detecting problems with mammographic units that can lead to missing results on invalid studies in this important health topic.

articleTitle: Effect of Polylactic Acid/Polycaprolactone Composite and Geometry on Simulated Stents Using Finite Element Analysis for the Treatment of Atherosclerosis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Conventional stents face challenges, prompting the need for alternatives like biodegradable stents made from resorbable polymers. This study examines the impact of stent cell geometry (Igaki-Tamai, Absorb, Elixir) and polylactic acid (PLA)/polycaprolactone (PCL) ratios on mechanical behavior. Finite element analysis revealed that Igaki-Tamai had the highest von Mises stresses, displacements, and strains, while Absorb showed uniformly low displacements across materials. Elixir geometry had the lowest maximum stresses and strains across all material concentrations.

articleTitle: Comparing Functional Connectivity Metrics from Resting-State fMRI: Applications to Alzheimer's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Resting-state functional connectivity, derived from resting-state functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging, maps neural patterns representing spontaneous brain activity. The choice of connectivity metrics could significantly impact the results and interpretations of the analysis. This study compares 10 commonly used metrics to the gold-standard Pearson Correlation measure using the Mantel test. This analysis was conducted using data from two popular public repositories, ADNI3**Data used in preparation of this article were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database (adni.loni.usc.edu). As such, the investigators within the ADNI contributed to the design and implementation of ADNI and/or provided data but did not participate in analysis or writing of this report. A complete listing of ADNI investigators can be found at: http://adni.loni.usc.edu/wpcontent/uploads/howtoapply/ADNIAcknowledgementList.pdf and OASIS3. Our findings showed that the Mantel test discriminates between metrics and reveals possible influences in connectivity patterns related to the datasets and cognitive groups. This comparative approach could identify measures that most diverge from Pearson Correlation. Based on these results, we propose a multi-feature framework for selecting relevant functional connectivity metrics in a data-driven manner, facilitating subsequent processing and analysis.

articleTitle: Development of the OptiSurge System for Surgical Times Measuring at Alma Máter de Antioquia Hospital
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Surgery represents approximately 60% of hospital revenue. However, improving service performance is challenging without a proper description of the problems to address. This study aimed to develop a surgical time measurement tool to identify the utilization rate of operating rooms and the compliance with the surgical schedule, thereby enhancing service performance. The research followed four stages: problem analysis and definition, innovation process using design thinking, solution design, and system testing in the surgical service. After 10 days of implementation, operating room utilization was 75.71%, and compliance with the surgical schedule ranged between 61.2% and 75.5%. The semi-automated units showed an error margin between 0.11% and 0.32%, while fully automated units had errors of 14.24% and 27.75% (electrosurgical unit and movement unit in the anesthesia machine, respectively). A tool was designed, focusing on nine key surgical moments: patient entry and exit, start and end of room preparation, surgery, anesthesia, and cleaning. While overall system performance was good, the accuracy of automated units could be improved. This system may represent the beginning of an innovative and easy-to-use technology to identify surgical problems and enhance hospital performance in Colombia.

articleTitle: Effect of Different MRI Modalities on Brain Tumor Segmentation Performance: A Study With BraTS2020 and 2D U-Net Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Gliomas are the most common form of primary brain malignancy in adults, with an incidence of approximately 5 cases per 100,000 inhabitants annually, and are known for their high morbidity and mortality. Glioblastomas, the most prevalent and aggressive form of gliomas, exhibit significant heterogeneity, including subregions such as peritumoral edema, necrotic foci, and active tumor. Effective diagnosis and treatment depend on accurate segmentation of these subregions. This study compares various combinations of imaging modalities for glioma segmentation using the 2D U-Net convolutional neural network (CNN) and the BraTS2020 dataset. Among the combinations tested, the T1ce_FLAIR model, which integrates T1-contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) sequences, achieved the highest Dice coefficients: 84.81% for peritumoral edema, 76.99% for enhancing tumors, and 72.25% for necrotic regions. This combination provided the most comprehensive tumor representation and demonstrated superior performance compared to other combinations of imaging modalities.

articleTitle: Development of Anatomical Models Using 3D Printing for Multiple Purposes in Medicine and Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Explore the multifaceted role of anatomical models in medicine, their development processes, and the revolutionary impact of 3D printing technologies in this field. We delve into the diverse applications of anatomical models, outlining the stages involved in their development for different parts of the human body, and highlighting the transformative potential of 3D printing in creating these models. By examining the intersection of traditional anatomical modeling techniques with cutting-edge 3D printing technologies, we aim to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state and future prospects of anatomical modeling in biomedical engineering.

articleTitle: Attention and Memory: Neural Relationships and Differences Using RSA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This research aims to explore a relatively new analysis methodology in the field of neuroscience called Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA). This methodology allows for the identification of relationships between brain representations of different natures, the generalization of results across multiple users, and even the comparison of electrophysiological results with behavioral data or computational model outcomes. Specifically, the goal is to uncover the underlying neural relationships between attentional and memory cognitive processes. A sample of 21 users had their brain electrical activity recorded during the performance of cognitive and memory tasks, which have been validated in the state of the art. These EEG signals were pre-processed to remove artifacts that could affect the study. Afterward, the signals were divided into frequency bands and segmented into seven time windows. For each of the 7 generated time windows, 38 power features and statistics moments were extracted to represent each EEG record. The results showed that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> frequency bands have a high monotonic correlation between attentional and memory processes. Additionally, considering the general cognitive processes and focusing only on their neural activation power features, no relationships between the two processes were observed. This indicates that their brain activation patterns are independent of each other.

articleTitle: A Myoelectric Signal-Based Classification System for Elbow Flexion Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: The control of prosthetics and exoskeletons has significantly advanced in recent years, improving the quality of life for individuals with amputations and motor disabilities through devices that mimic natural limb movements. This study investigates the classification of elbow flexion movements using myoelectric signals (MES) to develop efficient and reliable control systems. Utilizing classifiers such as Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), the research focuses on elbow flexion at angles of 0°, 30°, 60°, and 90°. The study collected myoelectric signals from the biceps brachii of eight able-bodied participants, with data acquisition involving 50-second cycle of rest and elbow flexion. Signal preprocessing involved digital filters to remove noise and artifacts, followed by feature extraction, including mean absolute value (MAV), zero-crossing rate (ZC), slope sign changes (SSC), integrated EMG (iEMG), and waveform length (WL). Results show that the classifiers achieve high accuracy, with RF demonstrating a more consistent performance across all angles with an overall accuracy of 65.42%, compared to SVM 59.45%. The highest individual accuracy achieved was 91%, highlighting the potential of these methods. The classifiers, however, showed reduced effectiveness when trained with combined data from all subjects and had notable difficulties in classifying movements at 30 degrees. This study confirms the efficacy of EMG signals for motion classification and highlights the importance of advanced filtering techniques and specific features. Additionally, the prediction response time of the system allows for the implementation of this classification process in real time using both classifiers.

articleTitle: Characterization of Electroencephalography (EEG) Responses to Musical Stimuli
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of different musical genres on electroencephalographic (EEG) responses in healthy subjects. The EEG technique was analyzed for five different music styles, such as classical, rock, jazz, vallenato, and urban, and in this way, to determine the influence in brainwave patterns. For instance, classical music was linked to alpha brainwave patterns associated with relaxation, while genres like rock and reggaeton are associated with beta patterns, indicating of concentration and mental activity. The study also explores how intrinsic factors such as musical lyrics and individual differences like musical training and preferences impact brain activity. Findings suggest that music can evoke strong emotional responses and activate different brain regions depending on the genre and individual factors. This complexity underscores the importance of considering personal and cultural aspects in understanding the neural dynamics of musical experiences.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Effect of Signal Quality on Sleep Stage Classification Using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Manual scoring is commonly employed in polysomnography (PSG) to record, score, and interpret physiological sleep data. This method analyzes multiple signals to detect disorders but is hindered by its time-consuming, particularly given the typical 8-hour sleep period, and is susceptible to intra-scorer variability, resulting in inconsistent outcomes. Automated methods are essential to enhance efficiency, consistency, and accuracy in PSG scoring. This study evaluates the impact of data quality on sleep stage classification using the Random Forest method. PSG signals were preprocessed and analyzed in Matlab, with feature extraction in the time and frequency domains, including signal amplitude and power spectral density in delta and beta bands. Features were selected based on criteria for classifying Rapid Eye Movement (REM) and Non- Rapid Eye Movement (NREM) stages. Results showed a 2.07% improvement in REM sensitivity a 0.22% increase in NREM sensitivity for high-quality data. This underscores the importance of measuring data quality in sleep stage classification, especially in less controlled environments like hospitals or homes.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition Using sEMG, Time-Frequency Analysis and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of improving prosthetic control through the analysis of electromyographic (sEMG) signals and gesture recognition. Using the Ninapro database [1] containing EMG signals from 10 subjects performing 17 different movements, focusing on recognizing 12 specific gestures. Each gesture was repeated six times per subject, resulting in a robust dataset for analysis. The methodology employed a combination of statistical techniques, arithmetic operations and Fourier transformations to preprocess and analyze the EMG signals. Various machine learning (ML) models were evaluated, with the RandomForest classifier achieving the highest accuracy at 20.8%, while other classifiers like KNeighbors, GaussianNB, SVM(Support Vector Machines), and MLP(Multi-Layer Perceptrons) showed lower performance. To improve the results, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied, but it only resulted in marginal improvements. Given the limitations of traditional ML methods, the EMG signals were converted into grayscale images and applied Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for frequency domain analysis. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on these images, achieving a high accuracy of 95% in gesture recognition. The CNN's performance underscores the potential of deep learning (DL) techniques in capturing complex patterns in sEMG signals, leading to significant improvements in real-time prosthetic control. This work contributes the foundation for future AI integration in biomedical applications, particularly in assistive technologies. Overall, this study highlights the effectiveness of artificial intelligence in assistive engineering through detailed exploration of sEMG signal processing and gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Prediction of Readmission Risk in Hospital Patients Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Hospital readmissions are a significant management challenge, with both clinical and economic implications. In this study, we apply artificial intelligence techniques to predict hospital readmissions in adult patients within 30 days of discharge using a dataset from Hospital Alma Máter de Antioquia, that includes demographic, clinical, and hospitalization information. The project tested several machine learning algorithms including logistic regression, decision trees and deep learning as neural networks. The results show that the neural network model achieved the best balance between the metrics of Specificity=84.0%, Precision=41.5%, Recall=98.7%, F1-Score=58.4%, accuracy=85.5% and AUC=94.7%. This study highlights the usefulness of artificial intelligence techniques for improving hospital readmission management.

articleTitle: Evaluating Lanthanide-Doped Carbon Dots for Sensing Glucose and pH Within the Concentration Range of Clinical Interest
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Monitoring glucose and pH levels is essential for tracking diabetes and preventing complications. Even though traditional sensing methods such as immunoassays, chromatog-raphy and wearables are effective, they still have limitations in the practicality, accessibility, and variability of fluid used for sensing. This research explores a different approach to developing a sensing platform for glucose and pH detection using carbon dots (CDs) doped with lanthanide ions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gd}^{3+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Yb}^{3+}$</tex>). Comparing fluorescence responses of three different nanoplatforms (CDs, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CDs}:\text{Gd}^{3+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CDs}: \text{Gd}^{3+}/\text{Yb}^{3+}$</tex>) at various pH and glucose concentrations within the concentration range of clinical interest of these analytes in biofluids such as blood serum, saliva, and urine, allows us to identify the most effective nanoplatforms: CDs for blood serum, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CDs}:\text{Gd}^{3+}$</tex> for saliva, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CDs}:\text{Gd}^{3+}/\text{Yb}^{3+}$</tex> for urine. Using a fixed excitation wavelength of 500 nm, significant fluorescence variations were evidenced within the control and variance between them. These early results are encouraging and allow for identifying potential new applications of CDs in the biomedical field, especially in the monitoring diseases such as diabetes and pH changes.

articleTitle: Real-Time Stress Detection Using Single-Lead ECG Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CIIBBI)
abstract: Stress detection is an active research field with ongoing challenges, particularly in real-time data analysis. This pilot study aims to implement a real-time stress detection algorithm that utilizes cardiac and respiratory information extracted from a single-lead ECG signal. Novel methods are combined to extract physiological indices, which are then processed using the XGBoost machine learning technique to provide per-second inferences. ECG signal processing is conducted over a storage buffer to ensure low processing time, with sliding-window analysis applied to extract cardiac indices in the time domain, frequency indices with the orthogonal subspace projection decomposition method, and respiratory indices in both time and frequency domains from ECG-derived respiration. A single-subject experiment, including a relaxation stage, musical stimuli stage, and stressor stage, is conducted to evaluate the algorithm's performance. The comparison between indices extracted via offline and real-time processing yielded a Pearson correlation coefficient average of 0.98 for 21 indices, demonstrating the method's effectiveness. Additionally, the stress probabilities inferred by the model during the experiment clearly distinguish between stages, as supported by visual descriptive statistics and significant differences found in ANOVA and post-hoc tests.
